newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: One killed in opposition's strike in Karachi.
newsitem.headline: One killed in opposition's strike in Karachi.

text.p: Gunmen killed a man and demonstrators burned two vehicles in Karachi on Sunday as a one-day strike called by opposition parties gripped the port city, police and witnesses said.
Mohammad Hassan, 35, was kidnapped before dawn and shot dead at a desolate place in Model Colony, police said. They said they were investigating his death and gave no other details.
It was not immediately known if the murder was tied to the strike.
The two vehicles were set on fire at Korangi in District East, apparently as a warning to drivers to keep their vehicles off the roads, police said.
Police said they gave chase to five people who torched the vehicles, and arrested and charged them with arson.
Meanwhile, the opposition-led strike squeezed Pakistan's normally bustling commercial hub. Witnesses said shopping centres, schools and colleges were closed and public transport was not running.
Government departments, airline offices at the Karachi airport, the port and railways were open, but attendance was thin due to the non-availability of transport, one witness said.
The Karachi stock exchange operates on Sundays, and dealers said it was likely to open mixed because of expected thin attendance.
The strike also slowed the movement of petroleum products, edible oils, and other food commodities to the countryside due to the fear of arson, one transport operator said.
But a police official said the strike was only partial and that shops were likely to open later in the day. He said most of the shops had closed their shutters for fear of violence.
Armed police and paramilitary rangers patrolled the city's violence-prone areas, witnesses said.
About 300 people have been killed in ethnic, sectarian and political violence so far this year in Karachi, far fewer than the 2,000 deaths recorded last year.

The nine-party opposition alliance, including the main Pakistan Muslim League and the ethnic Mohajir National Movement (MQM), called the strike to protest the killing by police of an MQM activist on Thursday.

Police said earlier that the activist, Mohammad Farooq, and other "terrorists" had attacked a police unit in Karachi's central Gulbhar area. Farooq was killed when police fired back and the others escaped.
The MQM seeks greater political and economic rights for Mohajirs, the Urdu-speaking Moslems who migrated from India when the subcontinent was partitioned in 1947, and their descendants.
